description: Jira Cloud issue tracking: read, create and edit issues, manage comments and links, and drive workflow transitions

contract.description: Read one Jira issue by key (`PROJ-123`) — summary, description, status, assignee, reporter and every other configured field. Hosted project admission requires a key rather than a numeric id. Returns Jira's full default field set, including custom fields, because narrowing it needs the `fields` query parameter this legacy catalog operation cannot encode. Text fields are wiki markup, not rich content

operations.description: Read one Jira issue by key (`PROJ-123`) — summary, description, status, assignee, reporter and every other configured field. Hosted project admission requires a key rather than a numeric id. Returns Jira's full default field set, including custom fields, because narrowing it needs the `fields` query parameter this legacy catalog operation cannot encode. Text fields are wiki markup, not rich content

changelog.description: Change history, when expanded. Not requested by this operation

expand.description: Comma-separated names of the parts that *could* be expanded — a hint, not data

fields.description: EVERY FIELD OF THE ISSUE, one level down — `summary`, `description`, `status`, `assignee`, `reporter`, `priority`, `issuetype`, `project`, `created`, `updated`, plus every custom field as `customfield_NNNNN`. Jira's schema declares no member of this map, because the members are whatever the site has configured, so nothing is enumerated here. `status` is a nested object (`{name, statusCategory}`), not a string, and text fields are wiki markup

id.description: The issue's numeric id, **as a string** — Jira returns ids as strings throughout

key.description: The issue key, e.g. `PROJ-123`. It changes if the issue moves project; the id does not

renderedFields.description: The same fields rendered to HTML, when asked for. Not requested by this operation

contract.description: Create a Jira issue in a project. Visible to everyone with access to the project and notifies its watchers. Only project, summary and issue type are set: a description cannot be sent yet (see the connector's notes), so file the detail as a comment afterwards. Returns the new issue's id, key and self URL

operations.description: Create a Jira issue in a project. Visible to everyone with access to the project and notifies its watchers. Only project, summary and issue type are set: a description cannot be sent yet (see the connector's notes), so file the detail as a comment afterwards. Returns the new issue's id, key and self URL

params.description: Key of the project to file the issue in, e.g. `PROJ`
params.name: project_key

params.description: One-line issue summary; this is the issue's title
params.name: summary

params.description: Name of the issue type as the project defines it, e.g. `Task`, `Bug` or `Story`
params.name: issue_type

id.description: The new issue's numeric id, as a string

key.description: The new issue's key, e.g. `PROJ-123`. This is what every following call addresses it by — nothing else in the response identifies it

transition.description: Present when the create asked for a transition: its own `{status, errorCollection, warningCollection}`. A failure here does not fail the create, so a `201` can still mean the transition did not happen

watchers.description: Same shape, for watchers the create asked to add

contract.description: Read the comments on a Jira issue, oldest first. Returns Jira's first default-sized page only: paging needs the `startAt` and `maxResults` query parameters this connector cannot encode, so an issue with a long discussion is truncated. Comment bodies are wiki markup

operations.description: Read the comments on a Jira issue, oldest first. Returns Jira's first default-sized page only: paging needs the `startAt` and `maxResults` query parameters this connector cannot encode, so an issue with a long discussion is truncated. Comment bodies are wiki markup

comments.description: The comments, oldest first. Bodies are Jira wiki markup

author.description: Who wrote it: `{accountId, displayName, active, self}` — an `accountId`, never a username, and `emailAddress` only where the site's privacy settings expose it

body.description: The comment text in wiki markup

created.description: Jira's own timestamp format, e.g. `2021-01-17T12:34:00.000+0000` — not RFC 3339 with a colon in the offset

id.description: The comment's id, as a string

jsdPublic.description: On Jira Service Management, whether the customer on the portal can see this comment. False is an internal note

renderedBody.description: The same body as HTML, when expanded

updateAuthor.description: Who last edited it, which need not be the author

visibility.description: Present when the comment is restricted to a role or group: `{type, value, identifier}`. Its absence means everyone who can see the issue can see the comment

maxResults.description: How many comments the page could hold, chosen by Jira

startAt.description: The offset this page starts at — 0 here, since this operation cannot send one

total.description: How many comments the issue has in total. **Greater than the length of `comments` means the discussion is truncated**, and this operation cannot fetch the rest

contract.description: Add a comment to a Jira issue. The comment is visible to everyone who can see the issue — including customers on a service-management portal — and notifies its watchers; restricting it to a project role or group is not supported yet. The body is Jira wiki markup (`*bold*`, `{code}`), not Markdown and not rich content

operations.description: Add a comment to a Jira issue. The comment is visible to everyone who can see the issue — including customers on a service-management portal — and notifies its watchers; restricting it to a project role or group is not supported yet. The body is Jira wiki markup (`*bold*`, `{code}`), not Markdown and not rich content

params.description: The comment text, in Jira wiki markup. Must not be blank
params.name: body

author.description: The account the token belongs to — a posted comment is attributed to it

body.description: The comment as stored, in wiki markup

id.description: The new comment's id, as a string

jsdPublic.description: On Jira Service Management, whether the portal customer can see it. Read it before treating a comment as internal

self.description: The comment's own API URL. There is no browser link in this response — a human-facing link has to be built from the issue key

visibility.description: Absent here, because this connector cannot restrict a comment. Absence means everyone who can see the issue can see it

contract.description: List the workflow transitions available on a Jira issue right now, with the id and target status of each. Call this before `jira-issue-transition`: transition ids are per-workflow, not global, and only the transitions valid from the issue's current status are returned

operations.description: List the workflow transitions available on a Jira issue right now, with the id and target status of each. Call this before `jira-issue-transition`: transition ids are per-workflow, not global, and only the transitions valid from the issue's current status are returned

expand.description: Expansion hint, absent from the vendor's example

transitions.description: The transitions available from the issue's **current** status. An empty array means the workflow offers none to this user right now — not that the issue is closed

fields.description: What a screen would ask for, keyed by field id, each with its own metadata including whether it is required. A required field here is the reason a transition can be listed and still be refused

hasScreen.description: True when Jira would show a form for this transition. It may then require fields this connector cannot send, and the call fails

id.description: The transition id to send as `transition_id`. Per-workflow, not global, and a string

isAvailable.description: Whether the transition can be executed now. Not present on every entry — the vendor's own examples omit it — so absence is not `false`

name.description: The transition's label as the workflow names it, e.g. `Done` or `Start Progress`. Match on this rather than hard-coding an id

to.description: The status the issue would land in: `{id, name, description, statusCategory}`, where `statusCategory` is `{id, key, name, colorName}` and its `key` is the coarse `new`/`indeterminate`/`done` grouping a flow can branch on

contract.description: Move a Jira issue through a workflow transition — the way an issue is closed, reopened or advanced. Get the transition id from `jira-issue-transitions-list` first; ids are per-workflow and only transitions valid from the current status are accepted. The status change is visible on every board showing the issue, notifies watchers, and may fire project automation. Answers `204` with an empty body on success

operations.description: Move a Jira issue through a workflow transition — the way an issue is closed, reopened or advanced. Get the transition id from `jira-issue-transitions-list` first; ids are per-workflow and only transitions valid from the current status are accepted. The status change is visible on every board showing the issue, notifies watchers, and may fire project automation. Answers `204` with an empty body on success

params.description: Id of the transition to perform, as returned by `jira-issue-transitions-list`, e.g. `31`
params.name: transition_id

contract.description: Read changed issues from one admitted project. Both Jira runtime placements build fixed JQL with updated >= unquoted epoch milliseconds, orders updated ASC then key ASC, and return safe issue projections. Personal gateway connections expose api_url and null browser_url; native tenant connections expose browser_url. Repeat the same window and opaque next_page_token until is_last; overlapping windows retain stable issue id plus updated revision. No JQL text is accepted.

contract.description: List permitted Jira projects through the native adapter, restricted to configured project keys. Follow next_start_at even when local policy removes every item in a provider page. Project id is stable; key and name are discovery metadata.

operations.description: List permitted Jira projects through the native adapter, restricted to configured project keys. Follow next_start_at even when local policy removes every item in a provider page. Project id is stable; key and name are discovery metadata.

contract.description: Read a bounded comment page for one admitted issue. Both runtimes return comments, start_at, max_results, total, is_last and next_start_at. Follow all offsets; timestamps retain Jira timezone syntax. Author identities are omitted. visibility and jsd_public preserve restriction evidence for downstream scope decisions; returned comments are visible to this principal, not necessarily company-public. Legacy comment-list is unchanged.
